analysis.title: GS Blekos - GS 2027 Outlooks / Global Equity Outlook / Global Macro Outlook / Nvidia / Siemens / Semicon Takes / Ottobock / Zealand / Global Transport / Europe Banks Tracker (13 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Global Equity Strategy 2027 Outlook: earnings growth is expected to slow sharply across all major regions as 2027 begins, AI capex growth is likely to peak, and the cost of capital remains elevated.

GS expects equities to keep rising in 2027 despite the slowdown, citing a sharp de-rating that has improved valuations, positive but slower nominal economic and earnings growth, and lower bond yields, inflation and oil prices. Volatility is expected to be high.
GS equity positioning for 2027: Growth balanced with selective Defensives and beneficiaries of lower bond yields.

GS Macro Outlook 2027: two more Fed hikes and one ECB hike are expected, with both returning to cuts in late 2027. Most GS forecasts for other central banks sit below market pricing, so longer-term rates are expected to fall modestly despite large government deficits and heavy AI-linked borrowing.

GS expects positive returns for equities and bonds in 2027, but with a bumpy path. The AI investment boom has had a much larger impact on earnings and market values than on GDP growth, and as the impulse peaks markets may question whether the record share of GDP going to US earnings can persist.
GS expects AI capex to still rise strongly in 2027, so positive earnings growth should cushion the transition. Financing needs from AI investment will likely keep pushing credit spreads wider.

Nvidia (NVDA) management transition: GS describes the situation as fluid with possible further information to come. Based on available information, GS expects a measured direct impact on Nvidia's financials and earnings power over the next 12-18 months, given a 12-24 month backlog and order book and a defined 2-3 year product roadmap already in execution.
Siemens AG after 4Q26: the CEO and CFO hosted a sell-side meeting in London. GS notes a strong start to fiscal FY27 in automation, with double-digit software growth expected for the year.
Siemens: data center growth visibility remains strong despite potential near-term order volatility and supply-chain dynamics.

Siemens: management intends to keep M&A discipline while prioritizing software assets, particularly in building services, plus selective hardware. Mobility is core to Siemens' AI strategy, and greater platform conformity is being enforced to protect segment margins.

SEMICON Europa (Munich, 11 Nov): GS visited the VAT Group and Ebara booths and met representatives there. GS also had unscheduled meetings with Pfeiffer Vacuum, Inficon and Edwards Vacuum (the vacuum technology division of Atlas Copco). The summary does not give the takeaways.

Ottobock (OBCK.DE): GS reiterates Buy after sharp underperformance following Q3 26 results, which it views as overdone, with reimbursement uncertainty in focus. GS cuts core revenue, EBITDA and EPS estimates by 0-6% across FY26/27/28e and lowers its 12-month target price to €65 from €75.

Ottobock: GS says management needs to give more clarity on the reimbursement challenges and confirm whether they are transitory or a structural shift, and to deliver consistent, predictable performance.
Zealand Pharma (ZELA.CO) 3Q26 review: glepaglutide EU approval is the near-term catalyst, and obesity newsflow is quieter for now.
Also listed in the note, with no content in the text: Global Transport, 'Around the World in 80 Charts: Tracking the US import cycle', and the Europe Banks Earnings Tracker covering ABN, KBC and UCG.
